content:
Question: What is Business Gro?

Casava's public Business Gro page (https://casava.com/business-gro), reviewed on 22 October 2026, headlines the product as "Grow your business with Business gro" and says customers can "Enjoy easy access to business loans, business insurance and free trainings."

The About section says: "With Business Gro, you have access to capacity building and relevant training that allows you to enjoy basic business continuity and financial protection whenever you encounter natural or unexpected events."

The page does not publish the policy wording, a schedule of covered events, exclusions, deductibles, sub-limits, or a sum insured. Those details are not confirmed by this page.

Question: What benefits does the Business Gro page list?

On https://casava.com/business-gro the "Enjoy amazing benefits" section lists these public descriptions:

- Get Insurance Always: "Get Insurance and access to loans from providers."
- Private Sector Benefits: "Trainings and educational content by professionals."
- Tools for Growth: "Scale your businesses by getting the right tools for faster growth."
- Grant Loans and More: "Get business support from the government."

A frequently asked question on the same page, "What does the insurance coverage of business gro afford customers?", is answered: "Business Gro offers small businesses access to a range of essential services, including Business Insurance, Educational Training, and Business Loans."

This is a product description. It does not state which events are insured, what is excluded, or how much would be paid for an incident.

Question: Who is eligible for Business Gro? Who is Business Gro for?

On https://casava.com/business-gro both "Who is business gro for" and "Who is eligible to apply for Business Gro?" are answered with the same sentence: "Small medium entrepreneurs with registered businesses on the SMEDAN platform are eligible to apply for Business Gro."

The page does not list exceptions to that eligibility rule.

Question: How much does Business Gro cost? How do I buy Business Gro?

The Business Gro FAQ on https://casava.com/business-gro answers "How do I buy business gro?" as follows: "To get Business Gro, you need to be a registered member of SMEDAN. Once you've completed your registration, Business Gro will be seamlessly integrated into your dashboard, adding significant value to your membership. With just a small monthly fee of N200, you enjoy full access."

This N200 monthly fee is the Business Gro price stated on that product FAQ. It is separate from the site-wide footer line about subscriptions starting at N600.

Question: Does Casava cost N600? What does the website footer say about price?

The footer on https://casava.com/business-gro says "Insurance that just works. Sign up in 90 seconds with an affordable monthly subscription, starting at N600." The same footer line appears on other Casava pages reviewed the same day, including Terms.

That sentence is general website marketing. It is not labelled as the Business Gro fee. The Business Gro FAQ on the same product page states a monthly fee of N200 for Business Gro. Do not treat N600 as the Business Gro price.

Question: How do I make a Business Gro claim?

The Business Gro FAQ on https://casava.com/business-gro answers "How do I make a claim?" as follows: "In order to initiate a claim, please notify us by sending an email to info@smedanregister.ng. Attach relevant documents, including photographic evidence of the incident and a breakdown of the cost of the items. Our claims process will begin promptly upon receipt."

This tells the customer how to start a Business Gro claim. It does not say the claim will be approved, how long assessment will take, or what amount will be paid. This chat cannot register the claim or receive photographs. The customer should use the email address above.

Question: What does Business Gro not cover? Where are the exclusions?

The Business Gro FAQ on https://casava.com/business-gro answers "How can I know what my policy does not cover?" as follows: "You can know the exclusions of your policy by carefully reviewing your policy document. After making your first premium payment, you will receive a comprehensive policy document providing detailed information about your coverage."

The policy document itself is not on the public page and is not in this knowledge base. Exclusions, sub-limits, and claim-assessment rules therefore cannot be confirmed from the public pages reviewed for this assistant.

Question: Can I change my hospital at any time on Business Gro?

The Business Gro page at https://casava.com/business-gro includes the question "Can I change my hospital at any time" and publishes this answer, which does not mention hospitals: "Simply login to your Casava account and click on the “ File Claim” button then follow the instructions. You can be sure of a response within 24 hours. Alternatively, you can visit claims.casava.co and follow the process highlighted."

The published answer does not explain whether Business Gro includes hospital treatment or whether a hospital can be changed. Do not turn that answer into a hospital-cover rule. The separate Business Gro claim instruction on the same page is to email info@smedanregister.ng.

Question: What does Casava's help centre say Business Gro includes? Does it mention fire or flood?

Casava's public help-centre article "What is Business Gro?" (https://casava1.zohodesk.com/portal/en/kb/articles/what-is-business-gro), reviewed on 22 October 2026, says Business Gro provides small businesses with tools and services needed to grow a successful business in Nigeria.

It says that with a monthly payment of 200 Naira, access includes:
- Business Insurance (Fire and Flood)
- Training
- Loans

It also says payment for Business Gro can be made monthly, quarterly, or annually, and that access requires registering an account on SMEDAN and activating benefits on that account. Further enquiries are directed to hello@casava.co.

Naming "Business Insurance (Fire and Flood)" describes the package in that article. The article does not list exclusions, limits, deductibles, waiting periods, or how a particular incident is assessed. It is not the policy wording, and it does not mean every fire or flood incident is payable.

source_title: How do I pay for Business Gro?
content:
Question: How do I pay for Business Gro? Is there a USSD code?

Casava's help-centre article "How do I pay for Business Gro?" (https://casava1.zohodesk.com/portal/en/kb/articles/how-do-i-pay-for-business-gro), reviewed on 22 October 2026, says there are two ways to pay:

1. USSD: Dial *6555# on an MTN line and follow the prompts on the mobile screen. The article says you will receive 2 SMS messages with further instructions to complete registration.
2. Web: After registering an account on the SMEDAN website, log in and click on "SMEDAN" benefits to activate benefits on the web. Payment is made online by card or transfer. Payment can be monthly, quarterly, or annually.

The article's closing enquiry line is awkwardly formatted on the page. The visible text includes both hello@casava.co and info@smedanregister.ng. The product page states the Business Gro claim email separately as info@smedanregister.ng, and the public website contact email as hello@casava.com.

Question: How fast does Casava pay claims? What does the claims page promise?

The public claims page https://casava.com/claims, reviewed on 22 October 2026, says "We pay claims in 48hours, or less" and "You won’t have to wait weeks to get your claims paid." The described steps are: tell Casava what happened; the claims engine runs a review; the claim is evaluated and you get paid within 48 hours. The page also says "File a claim anytime, anywhere. We get it approved. You get paid."

These are marketing statements on the general claims page. They are not Business Gro policy wording and are not confirmation that a specific incident will be approved or paid within 48 hours.

The same page introduces Haruna: "Meet Haruna, your claims partner. Haruna makes the claims process so much easier. Make a claim anytime, and receive a response in minutes." That is also marketing copy, not a service guarantee for a particular claim.

Question: What is HealthCash? These answers are about HealthCash, not Business Gro.

The following questions and answers are published on the general claims page https://casava.com/claims. They describe HealthCash. Do not apply them to Business Gro unless a Business Gro source says the same thing.

What is HealthCash? "HealthCash provides you with cash back, if you receive treatment at the hospital for minor injuries and / or permanent disability."

What are the requirements to sign up for HealthCash? "You must provide a government issued ID card e.g NIN, Voters card, Drivers license and International Passport."

How many times can I make a claim in a year? "You can make a claim as many times as possible. However, your claim must be to the tune of the total amount you are entitled to." The page does not state that entitlement amount.

Can my plan cover for another family member? "Your healthCash policy only covers you as the policyholder. Family members are not covered." This sentence is about HealthCash.

Is there a time limit to make a claim? "You are required to file a claim within 72 hours of the incident. If you fail to do so, your claim might be rejected." This 72-hour statement is on the HealthCash portion of the claims page. The Business Gro page does not state this deadline.

How do I make a claim? "Simply login to your Casava account and click on the “ File Claim” button then follow the instructions. You can be sure of a response within 24 hours. Alternatively, you can visit claims.casava.co and follow the process highlighted." The Business Gro product page instead tells customers to email info@smedanregister.ng to initiate a Business Gro claim.

Question: How do I register a claim on the Casava website?

The page https://casava.com/make-a-claim, reviewed on 22 October 2026, says: "Fill in the form below to register a claim with Casava. Our team will get back to you as soon as possible."

The page shows these contact details: hello@casava.com, +234 201 330 9618, WhatsApp +234 702 500 4444, and 17 Olosa Street, V.I, Lagos.

It does not list required documents. For Business Gro specifically, the product page says to email info@smedanregister.ng with photographic evidence and a cost breakdown. This assistant cannot submit the claim form.

Question: How do I contact Casava? Is Casava licensed?

Contact details shown on https://casava.com/business-gro and repeated on the claims, make-a-claim, terms, and privacy pages reviewed on 22 October 2026:
- Email: hello@casava.com
- Phone: +234 201 330 9618
- WhatsApp: +234 702 500 4444
- Address: 17 Olosa Street, V.I, Lagos

The Business Gro help-centre articles use hello@casava.co for further enquiries. That is a different domain from hello@casava.com on the website.

The footer states: "Casava Inc. is a Delaware, USA registered LLC Corporation. Casava Microinsurance Limited (CML) is registered in the Federal Republic of Nigeria and licensed by National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) to provide life and general microinsurance underwriting services."

Casava's public products linked from the site include Health Insurance, Health Cash, Business Gro, and Credit Life. The privacy policy contact block also lists Casava Microinsurance Limited, 17 Olosa Street, Victoria Island, Lagos 101241, hello@casava.com.

Question: What do Casava's website terms cover? What products are named?

The Terms and Conditions at https://casava.com/terms, reviewed on 22 October 2026, govern use of www.casava.com and affiliated websites and services operated by Casava Microinsurance Limited. They say the services offered under those terms include health insurance, health cash, Businessgro, and credit life products. They are website and account terms. They are not the Business Gro policy wording, and where the website conflicts with these terms, the terms prevail.

Casava says it may modify the terms and will notify customers before implementing changes. The terms are governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and disputes are subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of a competent court in Nigeria.

Account registration terms apply when a person opens an account and subscribes to a policy. A customer can close an account at any time at no cost by contacting Casava, but remains liable for obligations on the account. After closure they cannot access Casava services. Casava may close or suspend an account for reasons including regulatory non-compliance, breach of the terms, legal or fraud risk, or a legal requirement. The page says that list is not exhaustive. Casava is not obliged to refund premiums paid over time if an account is cancelled or suspended, except where the premium for a specific period is still active and the refund conditions apply.

Question: When can a Casava premium be refunded? What about the 50 naira card check, chargebacks, and hospital reimbursements?

From the Refund section of https://casava.com/terms, reviewed on 22 October 2026. These are account terms, not a promise about an insurance claim payout:

- Refund requests are entertained only if the insured is still on cover or if there was an overpayment.
- A premium can be refunded only while the policy is still active. The period of cover already used is calculated and deducted, and the balance is refunded. Premium is not refunded when the period of coverage has expired or has been used.
- If a premium was overpaid because of a technical glitch or human error, the customer may transfer the premium to the following month or request a refund of the excess, which the terms say is refunded to the account.
- A fifty naira (₦50) charge during onboarding as a card verification fee is immediately reversed to the bank account.
- A new customer who has not used any services on the policy and requests account closure within 15 days is entitled to a full refund of the premium.
- Refunds are processed through the same channel as the original payment and depend on verification checks.

Chargeback: if a customer asks their bank to reverse a payment because service was not rendered, Casava investigates. If service was not rendered for that payment, a reversal is approved. The terms say payment is made to the bank account within 3 to 7 working days, and that this may vary by bank.

Reimbursements: a reimbursement is when a customer pays out of pocket for health care at a hospital while Casava health insurance is still active, then requests a refund. Casava recommends not paying out of pocket unless a customer service representative has confirmed the benefit is not covered. The terms say customers are not eligible for reimbursements for payments made out of pocket for micro-service plans on Casava. This section is about health-care reimbursement, not a Business Gro property claim.

Question: What personal information does Casava say it collects?

Casava's privacy policy at https://casava.com/privacy-policy, reviewed on 22 October 2026, is issued by Casava Microinsurance Limited. It says personal information is processed in accordance with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and other Nigerian data protection regulations. "Services" include health insurance, health cash, businessgro, credit life, and other platforms Casava may use.

The policy says only minimum information required for the stated purposes should be collected. Categories named on the page include name, age, email, phone number, and other sensitive information such as marital status and religious affiliation; financial information such as Bank Verification Number (BVN) and credit-reference information; means of identification such as NIN, international passport, driver's licence, and voter's card; and health information such as smoker status or medical issues relevant to a policy or claim.

It also describes technical data such as IP address, device and browser data, usage data, and cookies. Collection methods listed include KYC forms, email and apps, claim forms, and live chat, chatbot, and profiler, among others. Information may also come from family members in cases of incapacitation or death for claims payment, credit reference agencies, hospitals, loss adjusters, and parties who help check that claims are eligible.

This assessment assistant is not Casava's official chatbot. It should not ask people to send NIN, BVN, card numbers, medical details, or claim photographs.

Question: What privacy rights does Casava describe, and how long is data kept? Who do I contact about privacy?

From https://casava.com/privacy-policy, reviewed on 22 October 2026. Casava says personal information is used for service delivery, personalisation, communication, legal and regulatory compliance, fraud and identity checks, and related purposes. It says information is not shared other than for purposes described in the policy. Recipients named include service providers, professional advisers, credit reference and fraud-detection organisations, financial organisations, and government agencies, only as far as needed for the specific purpose.

Rights named in the policy: access, rectification, erasure in certain circumstances, restriction of processing, data portability, objection to third-party marketing, and lodging a complaint. Casava says it may be unable to comply where another legal or regulatory duty applies.

The policy says industry-standard encryption is used in transit, and that a personal-data breach is reported to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission within 72 hours of Casava having knowledge of it, with notice to the data subject. Retention lasts only as long as needed for the policy purposes and legal requirements. Information may be stored or transferred outside Nigeria in the circumstances the policy lists, including consent and contract performance. Consent can be withdrawn, and withdrawal may affect access to features.

Privacy questions go to hello@casava.com. The policy asks the person to provide enough information for Casava to identify them. Postal contact on the policy: Casava Microinsurance Limited, 17 Olosa Street, Victoria Island, Lagos 101241.

The policy says claims and disputes about the policy are subject to the courts of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and that Casava shall not be liable for a breach claim that is not brought within one month of the date the breach arose. People should read the current policy on the website, because Casava says it may update the page.
